$reason: An `aria-hidden` takes an option out of the tree, on a wrapper above it or on the option itself, and an option in no tree needs no owner: axe asks nothing of either (measured, axe 4.13, which reads the value trimmed and in any case, ` TRUE` included). The wrapper's option is stamped by an inline `*ngIf`, in place, so the wrapper stays above it. What fails is the last option, shown, under a `list`. A reading that refused the hidden wrapper for its `aria-hidden`, a global attribute, or that read the value as written, or that took the inline template for one stamped elsewhere, or that asked only the ancestors and not the option, refused one of the first two instead.
